CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Individual Awards & Honors
Research Area — Player and coach honors beyond team titles
Headlined by Stephen Curry's retired jersey and decorated coaches; the program's depth shows in 35+ pro alumni and titles
in seven sports.
AT A GLANCE
Most famous honoree Stephen Curry ('06) — jersey retired by the school; later NBA MVP and
champion.
Coaching honors Football coach Jason Estep: 2x National Christian School Athletic
Association Coach of the Year; 2x Carolina Panthers Coach of the Week.
Program recognition Athletic Performance program is a four-time NSCA Strength of America
Award recipient.
Breadth State titles in seven sports plus 35+ pro alumni reflect a deep
individual-honors history.
Headline Individual Honors
Charlotte Christian's most prominent individual honor is the retirement of Stephen Curry's jersey ('06) — the
school formally honored its most famous alumnus, who went on to become an NBA MVP and multiple-time
champion. Across sports, the school's athletes have earned all-state, all-conference, and national
recognitions; the breadth is reflected in its 35+ professional alumni and state titles in seven sports (detailed
in the Professional Athletes and Championships documents). [Sources: Charlotte Christian; NBA.com]
Coaching Honors
• Jason Estep (football, 2007–2022) — 138–42 record with 8 NCISAA state titles; twice National Christian
School Athletic Association Coach of the Year; twice a Carolina Panthers Coach of the Week.
• Shonn Brown (boys basketball) — 400+ career wins; coached Stephen Curry; also serves as Upper
School Principal.
• Greg Simmons (baseball) — the program's beloved, long-tenured baseball coach who built a 17-title
power before his passing in 2023.
• [Sources: WCNC; The Charlotte Weekly; Charlotte Christian]
Program & Performance Recognition
The school's Athletic Performance (strength & conditioning) program is a four-time recipient of the NSCA's
Strength of America Award, recognizing commitment to safe, evidence-based athletic development.
[Source: Charlotte Christian Athletic Performance page]
Notes & Gaps
• Gatorade Players of the Year and McDonald's All-American honors specific to Charlotte Christian were not
confirmed in this pass; the strongest documented individual honors are Curry's jersey retirement and the
coaching awards above.
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1

CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Coaches, Pedigree & Continuity
Research Area — Leadership, coaching backgrounds, and program stability
Homegrown, long-tenured leadership: football's Chris James (alum) after Jason Estep (138–42, 8 titles); basketball's Shonn
Brown (400+ wins, coached Curry); the late Greg Simmons's baseball dynasty.
AT A GLANCE
Athletic Director Andrew Ross.
Head of School Barry Giller — also President of the NCISAA Board of Directors (a
governance leadership role).
Football Chris James (2008 CCS alum, ex-Richmond player) — took over in 2023
from Jason Estep (138–42, 8 state titles in 16 seasons).
Boys Basketball Shonn Brown — 400+ wins; coached Stephen Curry; also Upper School
Principal (long-tenured continuity).
Baseball legacy The late Greg Simmons built a 17-title baseball power.
Athletic Department Leadership
Charlotte Christian's athletics are led by Athletic Director Andrew Ross, within a school whose Head of
School, Barry Giller, also serves as President of the NCISAA Board of Directors — placing a Charlotte
Christian leader at the head of the state's governing body for independent-school athletics. [Sources:
Charlotte Christian Athletics; Charlotte Christian Leadership page]
Football — Chris James (head coach since 2023)
James is a 2008 Charlotte Christian alumnus who played under his predecessor before playing college
football at the University of Richmond and earning an exercise-science degree from UNC Charlotte. He was
on the CCS staff from 2010–2016, left to be the founding head coach at Covenant Day School, served as
offensive coordinator at Ardrey Kell and Myers Park, then returned as CCS offensive coordinator before
taking the head job in 2023 — a homegrown-continuity hire. In his second season (2025) the Knights
reached the NCISAA Division I state final. [Sources: WCNC; The Charlotte Weekly]
He succeeded Jason Estep, one of the most accomplished coaches in school history: 138–42 across 16
seasons (2007–2022) with 8 NCISAA state championships, two-time National Christian School Athletic
Association Coach of the Year, and a former Kansas City Royals strength coach who played baseball at
Eastern Kentucky. Estep coached 96 future college athletes and two future NFL draftees. [Sources: WCNC;
CoachComm; The Charlotte Weekly]
Boys Basketball — Shonn Brown
Shonn Brown is a continuity anchor: a 400+ win head coach who also serves as the school's Upper School
Principal, and who famously coached Stephen Curry during Curry's Charlotte Christian career. His dual role
as principal and long-tenured head coach reflects unusual program stability. [Sources: Shonn Brown
professional profile; Charlotte Christian]
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Baseball Legacy — Greg Simmons
The late Greg Simmons was the longtime varsity baseball head coach who built Charlotte Christian into the
NCISAA's most decorated baseball program (17 state titles). He passed away in January 2023 after a battle
with lung cancer; the program continues to honor his legacy. [Source: Charlotte Christian news]
Continuity & Stability — Summary
• Homegrown leadership: football coach Chris James and many staff are CCS alumni.
• Long tenures: Estep's 16-year football run, Brown's 400+ win basketball tenure (plus his principal role), and
Simmons's multi-decade baseball dynasty.
• Governance weight: the Head of School chairs the NCISAA board statewide.
Notes & Gaps
• Head-coach names for several non-flagship sports were not confirmed in this pass; the school's per-team
pages are the follow-up.
• Exact current titles/tenures can shift; verify the present football and basketball staff rosters before
recording.

harlotte-christian-football-coach/article_71a60fea-9db6-11ed-8c63-332aa01ffd72.html

Matriculation to NCAA Division I Athletics
Research Area — EVERY confirmed D1 commitment, 2014–2025, all conferences
(school-published list)
Comprehensive: includes all NCAA Division I commitments (any conference), not filtered to Power 4. Charlotte Christian's
own “Knights in College” list (2014–present) is the source.
AT A GLANCE
Scope ALL NCAA Division I commitments are included below, not just Power 4 —
Sun Belt, CAA, Southern, Big South, Ivy, AAC, Patriot, and other D1
conferences all count toward D1 matriculation.
School-published Charlotte Christian posts a complete “Knights in College” list by graduating
class (2014–present); D2/D3/NAIA signees exist too but are out of scope
for this D1-focused document.
Volume Roughly 100+ D1 signees across the 2014–2025 classes, once every
conference is counted (not just Power 4).
Breadth Football and baseball lead in raw numbers, but D1 commits span track &
field, baseball, softball, soccer, volleyball, lacrosse, golf, basketball,
swimming, wrestling, and rowing.

Ten/ACC/Big 12) names. Power 4 conferences are marked “(P4)” in the conference column so the two
views (all-D1 vs. Power-4-only) can both be read from one table. Non-D1 signees (D2, D3, NAIA, junior

Tally
Counting every row above, Charlotte Christian has sent well over 100 athletes to NCAA Division I programs
across the 2014–2025 classes once all conferences are counted, not just Power 4. Football and baseball
produce the most D1 signees by volume, but track & field, softball, baseball, soccer, volleyball, lacrosse,
golf, basketball, swimming, wrestling, and rowing are all represented. The Sun Belt, CAA, Big South,
Southern, and AAC conferences appear repeatedly — reflecting strong mid-major Division I placement
alongside the Power 4 names — and three Ivy League commitments (Yale, Dartmouth x2, Cornell) reflect
the school's academic profile.
Notes & Gaps
• Conference labels reflect each program's known D1 conference; a few programs (e.g., Butler football,
which plays non-scholarship FCS football in the Pioneer League) are technically D1 but non-scholarship —
noted where known.
• A handful of activities on the school's list (e.g., cheer, dance, acro & tumbling) are sponsored by the host
institution but may not be NCAA-championship sports in the traditional sense; they are included as
published by the school.
• The school's list does not always distinguish scholarship vs. walk-on status; that detail is noted only where
the source specified it (e.g., “walk-on” for Mac McLennan).
• D2, D3, and NAIA signees from the same classes exist on the school's full list but are intentionally
excluded here since this document's scope is Division I matriculation specifically.

CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Athletic Facilities & Infrastructure
Research Area — Grounds by sport, buildings, and what's next per the Master Campus
Plan
Sourced from the school's Master Campus Plan: outdoor grounds for football/track, soccer/lacrosse, tennis, baseball, and
softball, plus the Harvick & Warner field houses, Guy Gym, and the planned 53,000+ sq ft Saleh Athletic Center.
AT A GLANCE
Campus ~54-acre wooded campus in southeast Charlotte (7301 Sardis Road).
Outdoor athletic Harvick Field House, Guy Field (turf), and 8 tennis courts — opened Nov
complex 2022 for soccer, lacrosse, and tennis.
Track & football/soccer Renovated athletic stadium with new synthetic turf and a new track (2015).
stadium
Baseball & softball Greg Simmons Field (baseball, named for the late longtime coach) and a
separate dedicated softball field.
Coming next The planned Saleh Athletic Center — 53,000+ sq ft with a new main gym,
athletic performance center, and wrestling room.
Campus Overview
Charlotte Christian sits on roughly 54 wooded acres in southeast Charlotte (7301 Sardis Road). The
school's published Master Campus Plan lays out a multi-phase, multi-year buildout of academic and athletic
facilities, several of which are athletics-specific and already complete. [Source: Charlotte Christian Master
Campus Plan]
Outdoor Grounds by Sport
Sport Grounds / Venue
Football / Soccer / Track Main athletic stadium — renovated in summer 2015 with new synthetic turf and a new track.
This is the home venue for football and track & field, and doubles as a soccer venue.
Soccer / Lacrosse Guy Field — an artificial-turf field opened November 2022 as part of the new
northern-campus athletic complex, used by the soccer and lacrosse programs (and, for
halftime activities, golf).
Tennis Eight tennis courts, part of the same November 2022 athletic complex.
Baseball Greg Simmons Field — named for the school's longtime, beloved varsity baseball head
coach, who passed away in January 2023 after building the program's 17-title dynasty.
Softball A separate, dedicated softball field on campus.
Swimming No on-campus pool/natatorium was identified in this research pass; the team's home training
and meet venue was not confirmed — see Notes & Gaps.
Cross Country Uses the on-campus grounds and stadium area; specific course details were not published.
Golf No dedicated on-campus course; golf programs typically use a partner club (not confirmed
by name in this pass).
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Sport Grounds / Venue
Wrestling Practices in the Warner Field House multipurpose room (shared with cheerleading and other
uses); a dedicated wrestling room is planned for the new Saleh Athletic Center.
[Source: Charlotte Christian Master Campus Plan; Knights In Action athletics page]
Indoor & Support Buildings (Athletics-Specific)
• Harvick Field House (Nov 2022) — locker rooms for the soccer and tennis programs, bathrooms, a
concession stand, and a trainer's room; part of the new northern-campus athletic complex alongside Guy
Field, the tennis courts, a connecting loop road, and additional parking.
• Warner Field House (broke ground May 2012) — 7,800 square feet; houses athletic offices, a
multipurpose room used by wrestling, cheerleading, fine arts, and large-group meetings, locker rooms for
football, lacrosse, and wrestling, and a classroom used for PE lectures, team meetings, and study halls.
• Guy Gymnasium expansion (2012, concurrent with Warner Field House) — added 2,400 square feet to
accommodate double-court space for basketball and volleyball, plus expanded spectator seating. (The
basketball home court is referred to elsewhere as the Lamb/Johnson Gymnasium — the gym where
Stephen Curry played — likely the same facility under a court-naming convention; this should be confirmed
directly with the school.)
• [Source: Charlotte Christian Master Campus Plan]
Strength & Performance Facility
• A 5,400-square-foot weight room featuring 8 powerlift racks and Olympic weightlifting platforms.
• All strength and conditioning programs use ground-based, multi-joint movements with bars, free weights,
and bodyweight exercises, periodized to competition seasons.
• The program is a four-time recipient of the NSCA Strength of America Award.
• [Source: Charlotte Christian Athletic Performance / Charlotte Sports Performance pages]
What's Coming Next: the Saleh Athletic Center
The Master Campus Plan's next major athletics project is the Saleh Athletic Center, planned to exceed
53,000 square feet. As described by the school, it “will serve as a vibrant gathering place for everyone,”
featuring the school's main gymnasium, an athletic performance center, a wrestling room, a multipurpose
meeting space, locker rooms, a Hall of Honor, a school store, and concession areas. The school states the
broader plan (including this center and a rebuild of the middle and upper schools) is targeted for completion
by the time current kindergartners reach the upper school. [Source: Charlotte Christian Master Campus
Plan]
Game-Day & Broadcast Infrastructure
The athletic department supports livestreaming and online ticketing (via the school's Tickets & Livestream
hub) and has invested in game-day technology — including Division-I-grade wireless sideline
communication systems for football. [Sources: Charlotte Christian Tickets & Livestream; CoachComm]
Notes & Gaps
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 2
CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
• No on-campus swimming pool/natatorium was identified for Charlotte Christian in this pass. Many
Charlotte-area independent schools without their own pool train and host meets at an off-campus or club
facility (e.g., a city aquatic center or swim club); the swim team's specific home venue should be confirmed
directly with the school before stating it on-air.
• Golf's home course/practice facility was not identified by name.
• The exact relationship between the “Guy Gymnasium” (per the Master Campus Plan) and the
“Lamb/Johnson Gymnasium” (referenced in alumni/media coverage of Stephen Curry) was not fully
reconciled — they may be the same building with a named center court, which is a common convention,
but this should be verified.
• Seating capacities for the stadium and gymnasium were not published in the sources reviewed.

CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
High School NIL Landscape & Charlotte Christian's
Position
Research Area — NIL rules and how they apply
Charlotte Christian competes in the NCISAA, which permits NIL. Covers the policy framework and the school's position (incl.
its Head of School chairing the NCISAA board). No specific dollar deals are public.
AT A GLANCE
Affiliation Charlotte Christian competes in the NCISAA, which APPROVED an NIL
policy effective 2024–25.
Advantage window NCISAA athletes could pursue NIL in 2024–25 while NC public-school
athletes legally could not (until July 1, 2025).
Governance tie Charlotte Christian's Head of School, Barry Giller, is President of the
NCISAA Board — the body that adopted the NIL policy.
Honest limit No specific Charlotte Christian athlete NIL deals or dollar figures are
publicly disclosed.
The NCISAA NIL Policy (Applies to Charlotte Christian)
In February 2024 the North Carolina Independent Schools Athletic Association — which governs roughly
94–100 private schools including Charlotte Christian — approved a policy allowing its student-athletes to
profit from their name, image, and likeness while retaining eligibility, effective the 2024–25 school year.
[Sources: HighSchoolOT; On3]
Key rules:
• NIL activity must be kept SEPARATE from interscholastic participation; athletes may not use the school's
name/marks or appear in uniform in NIL deals.
• Prohibited categories include cannabis, alcohol, gambling, adult entertainment, drugs, and tobacco.
• All NIL agreements must be reported to and approved by the NCISAA state office.
• School personnel may not use NIL to recruit/enroll students or act as an athlete's agent.
• [Sources: On3; Lewis Brisbois sports-law analysis]
The Contrast: NC Public Schools
Public-school NIL took the opposite path: blocked by the legislature, banned by the State Board of
Education in June 2024, and only made permanently legal on July 1, 2025 (Brandon v. State Board of
Education; SB 563, creating an NC NIL Clearinghouse and a 50% business tax credit). For about a year,
NCISAA schools like Charlotte Christian had an NIL window their public-school counterparts did not.
[Sources: HighSchoolOT; RallyFuel NC NIL guide]
Charlotte Christian's Specific Position
Charlotte Christian is positioned to benefit from NIL in the same structural way as its NCISAA peers, with a
notable governance angle: its Head of School, Barry Giller, serves as President of the NCISAA Board of
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Directors — the very body that adopted the NIL policy. With a deep stable of high-profile athletes and a
famous alumni brand (Curry), the school's athletes are well-placed for NIL opportunity, though no specific
deals are public. [Sources: Charlotte Christian Leadership; On3]
Notes & Gaps
• No itemized list of Charlotte Christian athletes' NIL deals or dollar amounts was found — this document
covers the policy landscape and the school's structural position, not a deal-by-deal ledger (high-school NIL
deals are generally not disclosed and NCISAA filings are not public).

sections.text:
CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
National Profile (Football & Basketball)
Research Area — The school's dual-sport national identity
Charlotte Christian is a genuine two-sport national name: an NBA pipeline (Stephen Curry et al.) and a 9-time
state-champion football program that reached the 2025 D-I final.
AT A GLANCE
Dual identity Charlotte Christian is a genuine two-sport national name — football AND
basketball.
Basketball Produced Stephen Curry (and Seth Curry, Anthony Gill, Todd Fuller) — an
outsized NBA pipeline for a school its size.
Football A 9-time NCISAA state champion that reached the 2025 Division I state
final; beat national-power Rabun Gap-Nacoochee 55–48 in the 2025
playoffs.
National schedule Football regularly plays national/out-of-state and top public-school
opponents.
Why This Segment Covers Both Sports
Unlike schools with a single marquee sport, Charlotte Christian has a legitimate national profile in BOTH
football and basketball, so this segment covers both. [Source: Charlotte Christian Knights Accolades;
MaxPreps]
Basketball — an NBA Incubator
Charlotte Christian's basketball reputation is national, anchored by the fact that it produced Stephen Curry
— now one of the most famous athletes in the world — along with fellow NBA players Seth Curry and
Anthony Gill and 1996 NBA lottery pick Todd Fuller. National media (from the NBA to Medill/Northwestern to
MaxPreps) have profiled the school as the place where Curry's career began, and the school has retired his
jersey. For a school of ~1,300 students, that NBA output is extraordinary. [Sources: NBA.com; Medill
Reports; Wikipedia; MaxPreps]
Football — a Perennial NCISAA Power
• Nine NCISAA state championships (1992, 2008, 2012–14, 2017–20) — including back-to-back-to-back
runs.
• Reached the NCISAA Division I state championship game in 2025 (state runner-up) under coach Chris
James.
• A deliberately national/tough schedule: 2025 included reigning South Carolina 5A D-2 champion
Northwestern, Charlotte-area public powers (Independence, Myers Park), and a 55–48 playoff win over
national-power Rabun Gap-Nacoochee (GA).
• A pro/Power 4 pipeline: NFL alumni (Garrett Bradbury, Matthias Farley, Des Lawrence) and recent Power
4 signees (Georgia, Notre Dame, Iowa, NC State).
• [Sources: Charlotte Christian Knights Accolades; HighSchoolOT; SI/SBLive; MaxPreps]
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
The Combined Story
The through-line is that Charlotte Christian competes — and wins — at a high level across multiple sports
while sending alumni to the highest levels (NBA, NFL, MLB, MLS). Its national profile is less about a single
dominant team and more about sustained, broad excellence and a remarkable professional pipeline.
[Sources: as cited]
Notes & Gaps
• National team-ranking numbers (MaxPreps/On3 national polls) were not pinned to a dated snapshot here;
cite a specific poll/date if used on-air.
• The basketball national profile rests heavily on alumni (esp. Curry) rather than current national team
rankings; frame accordingly.

Research Area — On-site care and year-round performance
Credentialed athletic trainers (Dr. Kaitlynn Seymour, Madison Sitton) and a four-time NSCA Strength of America
performance program (Kyle Jacksic, Cami Roy) with a 5,400 sq ft facility.
AT A GLANCE
Athletic trainers Head AT Dr. Kaitlynn Seymour (DPT, ex-Coastal Carolina football AT) and
Madison Sitton, ATC.
Sports performance Director Kyle Jacksic (MS human performance) and coach Cami Roy; a
four-time NSCA Strength of America Award program.
Facility 5,400 sq ft weight room (8 power racks, Olympic platforms).
Internship A collegiate-style Athletic Performance Internship Program develops
aspiring professionals.
Model Multi-disciplinary: strength & conditioning, sports medicine, nutrition, and
sport psychology.
Athletic Training & Sports Medicine
Charlotte Christian's sports-medicine staff is led by Head Athletic Trainer Dr. Kaitlynn Seymour, who joined
after two years as the head football athletic trainer at Coastal Carolina University. She holds a Doctorate in
Physical Therapy from Emory University (2019) and a Master's in Athletic Training from Lenoir-Rhyne
(2021), is a certified and NC-licensed athletic trainer, and holds certifications in dry needling, IV, and CPR.
She is joined by athletic trainer Madison Sitton, who holds a Bachelor's in Exercise Science and a Master of
Science in Athletic Training. [Source: Charlotte Christian Athletic Forms / staff page]
The department emphasizes prompt injury reporting, thorough on-site evaluation, evidence-based
concussion assessment, individualized rehabilitation, functional testing, and physician clearance before
return to play — with ongoing continuing education at local, state, and national meetings. [Source: Charlotte
Christian sports-medicine protocols]
Sports Performance (Strength & Conditioning)
The Athletic Performance program is a four-time NSCA Strength of America Award recipient and uses
state-of-the-art technology to monitor and assess performance. Its multi-disciplinary Sports Performance
team spans strength & conditioning, sports medicine, sport nutrition, and sport psychology — a holistic,
college-style model. [Source: Charlotte Christian Athletic Performance page]
• Kyle Jacksic — Director of Athletic Performance (joined 2024). Bachelor's in exercise physiology
(University of Lynchburg); Master's in human performance (Canisius University) with a dual focus in
strength & conditioning and cardiac rehabilitation.

exercise science and Master's in Health, Human Performance & Recreation from Pittsburg State, where
she was a cross country/track captain.

multi-joint training, periodized to competition seasons.
• Internship program: a collegiate-style curriculum giving aspiring professionals hands-on coaching

CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Sports Offered at Charlotte Christian School
Research Area — Complete catalog of interscholastic sports and teams
Charlotte Christian School — Charlotte, NC · Mascot: Knights · Colors: Maroon, Gold & White · NCISAA 4A / CISAA ·
Founded 1950, grades JK–12.
AT A GLANCE
Sports offered 22 sports for boys and girls.
Teams Over 50 teams across middle school, junior varsity, and varsity levels.
Participation More than 80% of students in grades 7–12 play school-sponsored
athletics.
Affiliation NCISAA 4A division; member of the CISAA conference.
Founded / campus Independent, interdenominational Christian school founded 1950; ~54-acre
campus, grades JK–12.
Overview
Charlotte Christian School is an independent, co-educational, interdenominational Christian
college-preparatory school in southeast Charlotte (7301 Sardis Road), founded in 1950 and serving roughly
1,300 students from junior kindergarten through grade 12 on a 54-acre wooded campus. The athletic
department, whose teams are the Knights (maroon, gold, and white), states that it offers 22 sports for boys
and girls and fields more than 50 teams at the middle school, JV, and varsity levels, with more than 80
percent of students in grades 7–12 participating in school-sponsored athletics. [Sources: Charlotte Christian
Knights Accolades page; CoachComm school profile]
Charlotte Christian competes in the 4A division of the North Carolina Independent Schools Athletic
Association (NCISAA) and is a member of the Charlotte Independent Schools Athletic Association (CISAA),
alongside other leading Charlotte-area independent schools. [Source: Charlotte Christian Knights Accolades
page]
Complete List of Sports (all 22)
Charlotte Christian states that it offers 22 sports for boys and girls. The complete enumeration below —
counting boys' and girls' programs separately, as the school does — is drawn from the MaxPreps Charlotte
Christian sport index and the school's team pages, with Dance confirmed by the school's
state-championship list. Each is offered at the varsity level; most also field JV and middle school teams.
[Sources: MaxPreps Charlotte Christian Knights; charlottechristian.com Teams & Schedules; Knights
Accolades]

State & National Recruiting Rankings
Research Area — Students earning top recruit rankings
A dual-sport recruiting school; confirmed current recruit (L.J. Porter) plus a steady Power 4 signee history.
AT A GLANCE
Current recruit L.J. Porter — a 2026 top-NC football recruit listed at Charlotte Christian
(per the 247Sports NC rankings).
Dual-sport history Charlotte Christian produces ranked recruits in BOTH football and
basketball (Stephen Curry was famously underranked out of CCS).
Pipeline proof Repeated Power 4 signees (Georgia, Notre Dame, Iowa, NC State) confirm
a steady flow of ranked talent.
Primary services 247Sports / On3 / Rivals (football); the school also has an On3 program
page.
What “Top-100” Means Here
247Sports, On3, and Rivals publish state and national recruit rankings, primarily for football and basketball.
Charlotte Christian appears regularly in North Carolina's football rankings and has an On3 program page; it
is a genuine dual-sport recruiting school. [Sources: 247Sports NC football rankings; On3 Charlotte Christian
page]
Confirmed Recruiting Markers
• L.J. Porter — listed among the 2026 Top Football Recruits in North Carolina (247Sports) as a Charlotte
Christian player.
• Stephen Curry — the program's most famous recruiting story: lightly recruited out of Charlotte Christian
(no major-conference scholarship offers) before becoming an NBA legend — a frequently cited “rankings
miss” (MaxPreps has run features on the point guards ranked ahead of him).
• Power 4 signees as ranking proxies: recent classes sent players to Georgia, Notre Dame, Iowa, NC State,
Duke, and Wake Forest (see D1 Matriculation), indicating consistent ranked talent.
• [Sources: 247Sports; MaxPreps; Charlotte Christian Knights Accolades]
Notes & Gaps
• Specific numeric composite rankings (state/national) per current Charlotte Christian recruit were not all
pinned down in this pass; the 247Sports/On3 player pages are the follow-up for exact ranks.
• Basketball recruiting rankings for current Knights were not individually confirmed here — a potential area to
deepen.

CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Team Win-Loss Records — Recent Seasons
Research Area — Records and results, strongest for football and basketball
Covers the school's top 5 sports — Football, Basketball, Baseball, Softball, and Track & Field — with both boys' and girls'
programs included wherever both exist and data is available.
AT A GLANCE
Top 5 sports Football, Basketball (Boys & Girls), Baseball, Softball, and Track & Field
(Boys & Girls) — selected by championship history and recent prominence.
Football 2025 7–6; reached the NCISAA Division I state championship game (state
runner-up); beat Rabun Gap-Nacoochee 55–48 in the semifinals.
Basketball 2025–26 Boys: 7–20 in 2024–25, then reached the 2025–26 NCISAA 4A state final
(runner-up). Girls: 4 NCISAA titles historically (2000, 2002, 2003, 2004);
current-season record not confirmed.
Baseball The program's all-time most decorated sport — 17 NCISAA state titles
(1991–2022).
Softball & Track Softball: 3 state titles incl. 2025. Track & Field: Boys state champion 2025;
Girls placed 3rd at the 2025 NCISAA D1 meet.
How to Read This Document
Per the standard workflow, this document covers Charlotte Christian's top 5 sports by championship history
and recent prominence: Football, Boys Basketball, Baseball, Softball, and Track & Field. Records were
assembled from MaxPreps game logs, NCISAA brackets, the school's own championship list, and North
Carolina sports media. Football and boys basketball have the most detailed game-by-game data; baseball,
softball, and track have confirmed championship/title-season facts but full season-by-season W-L totals
were not all consolidated in this pass (noted under Gaps).
1. Football (Varsity) — 2025 Season
The Knights finished 7–6 and made a deep playoff run to the NCISAA Division I state championship game,
where they finished state runner-up. Quarterback Elliott Newcomb and running back Jamal Rule led the
offense. [Sources: MaxPreps Charlotte Christian football; HighSchoolOT]
Date Opponent Result Note
Nov 7, 2025 Charlotte Country Day W 36–0 NCISAA D-I Playoffs, Round 1
Nov 14, 2025 Rabun Gap-Nacoochee W 55–48 NCISAA D-I Playoffs (semifinal round)
Nov 21, 2025 State final opponent L 6–42 NCISAA D-I State Championship Game
Charlotte Christian also opened 2025 with a challenging non-conference slate including reigning South Carolina 5A Division 2
champion Northwestern and Charlotte-area public powers (Independence, Myers Park). [Source: SI/SBLive 2025 schedule]
2. Basketball — Boys & Girls (Varsity)
Compiled June 17, 2026. Sources cited inline and listed at end of each document. Page 1
CHARLOTTE CHRISTIAN SCHOOL KNIGHTS — ATHLETICS RESEARCH DOSSIER Charlotte, NC
Boys (2024–25): 7–20 overall, 0–10 in conference play (6th place). Boys (2025–26): improved to reach the
NCISAA 4A state championship game (state runner-up). Playoff/late-season results: beat Charlotte Country
Day 77–58; beat Covenant Day 53–50; narrow regular-season losses to two CISAA rivals (66–72 and
71–87); lost the 4A state final to Wesleyan Christian Academy 59–78. Key players included Marshall
Nicholson and Carter Burns. [Source: MaxPreps Charlotte Christian boys basketball]
Girls: the program has a strong historical pedigree (4 NCISAA state titles: 2000, 2002, 2003, and 2004, per
the school's own Knights Accolades page). Recent-season results include a loss to a CISAA opponent
(Charlotte Country Day) in January 2026. A full current-season overall win-loss record was not confirmed in
this research pass. [Source: Charlotte Christian Knights Accolades page; MaxPreps Charlotte Christian girls
basketball]
3. Baseball (Varsity) — Program Record
Baseball is Charlotte Christian's most decorated program of all time: 17 NCISAA state championships
(1991, 1999, 2000, 2002–2007, 2009, 2012–2015, 2019, 2021, 2022) — by far the most titles in any sport at
the school. The program produced 2023 College of Charleston-bound MLB pick Bailey Ober, plus Daniel
Bard, Luke Bard, and Jackson Kowar (see Professional Athletes). Longtime coach Greg Simmons built and
sustained this dynasty before his passing in January 2023. [Source: Charlotte Christian Knights Accolades
page]
A specific game-by-game win-loss record for the most recent (2025/2026) baseball season was not confirmed in this research pass
— see Notes & Gaps.
4. Softball (Varsity) — Recent Championship Run
Softball has emerged as a current power, winning NCISAA state titles in 2021, 2022, and 2025 — three
championships in five years. Anna Hinde ('25) signed with Florida State (ACC) off this roster. [Sources:
Charlotte Christian Knights Accolades page; Knights Accolades — Knights in College]
A specific game-by-game win-loss record for the 2025 championship season was not confirmed in this research pass — see Notes
& Gaps.
5. Track & Field — Boys & Girls
Boys: won an NCISAA state championship in 2025, adding to an earlier title in 2001. Girls: placed 3rd at
the 2025 NCISAA Division I championship meet (78 points), led by double-event winner Nina Dominique
(100m and 200m) and double-event winner Alesia Sylveraine (discus and shot put); the girls' anchor leg also
won the 4x100m relay. The girls' program has won earlier state titles in 2001 and 2002. Track scoring is by
meet placement rather than a traditional win-loss record. Evan Boykin ('25) signed with Kentucky (SEC) off
the boys' program. [Sources: Charlotte Christian Knights Accolades page; HighSchoolOT 2025 NCISAA D1
girls track & field results]
Notes & Gaps
• Football and boys basketball have confirmed game-by-game results for their most recent seasons;
baseball, softball, girls basketball, and both track & field programs have confirmed
championship/placement facts (years, signees, meet results) but exact season win-loss totals were not
confirmed for every program in this pass — MaxPreps' per-sport season pages are the recommended
follow-up.
